eyebrow: Why a policy document isn't a standard

steps.label: A document works for five teams
steps.sub: the ones who read it carefully when it was written

steps.label: It fails team number 212
steps.sub: hired 18 months later, who has never seen it

steps.label: The fix: move it into the template
steps.sub: a team gets the requirement the moment they call it — no reading required

code:
# the required job lives inside the shared template:
jobs:
  build-test-scan:
    steps:
      - name: Required security scan
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high

# GitHub -> Settings -> Branches -> Branch protection rule
# Require status checks to pass before merging:
#   [check] run-shared-pipeline / build-test-scan
caption: The question becomes "can anyone merge without this job green" — not "did they remember."

code:
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      skip-scan-reason:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""

jobs:
  build-test-scan:
    steps:
      - name: Required security scan
        if: inputs.skip-scan-reason == ''
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high
      - name: Scan skipped - reason on record
        if: inputs.skip-scan-reason != ''
        run: echo "::warning::Scan skipped: ${{ inputs.skip-scan-reason }}"
caption: A narrow, logged escape hatch — not a silent one, and not zero exceptions.
